SCOPE OF WORK
The Administrative Law Judges (ALJs) from the State of California, Department of General
Services (DGS), Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH) conduct administrative hearings in
accordance with Government Code sections 11500 et seq., other applicable statutes, and
pursuant to contracts and interagency agreements with other state and local entities. OAH is
required to provide American Sign Language (ASL) interpreter services for hearings at the
request of a party (Cal. Code Regs., tit. 5, § 3082 (d)). In addition, OAH must provide ASL
interpreter services for a hearing, upon request, for applicants, participants, members of the
public and companions, per the Americans with Disabilities Act (28 C.F.R. § 35.160).
1. AGREEMENT SUMMARY
A. Upon request, Contractor shall provide language professionals, equipment, materials
and tools required for OAH proceedings (i.e., committees, conferences, mediations and
hearings) for the following:
1) ASL Interpreting Services:
a. Onsite/In-person ASL Interpreters throughout the State of California
b. Video/Remote interpreting (VRI)
B. OAH is awarding two contracts for these services: a Primary Contract, and a Secondary
Contract. This contract is for the Secondary Contractor.
C. This contract is subject to Data Processing and Protection as outlined in Exhibit E and
has additional provisions for specific OAH case types as identified in Exhibit F and its
attachments.
D. On-site/In-person ASL interpreter services shall take place at an OAH office location
and at other locations in the State of California as set by OAH. OAH office locations are
identified in Exhibit A, Attachment 1. Other locations may include regional centers
(nonprofit corporations under contract with the Department of Developmental Services),
school district offices, and other state or local agency office locations.
E. OAH will have the sole option to extend the contract term for one (1) one additional year
at the contracted rates. The Contractor’s rates, Exhibit B, Attachment 1, will stay in
effect for the entire contract term, including the above referenced exercised option year.

B. Contractor agrees SharePoint sites are only for the exchange of information between

A. The State's normal business hours are: Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.
(PT), excluding observed State holidays. All scheduled services under this Agreement
shall be completed within normal business hours unless otherwise stated in the request

1) The length of hearings will vary from two (2) hours to several weeks and in rare

2) The State will pay a minimum of two (2) hours of scheduled ASL interpreting
services.
B. Current observed State holidays are: New Year's Day, Martin Luther King, Jr. Day,
Presidents’ Day, Cesar Chavez Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day,
Veterans Day, Thanksgiving Day, Day after Thanksgiving and Christmas Day.
C. Contractor shall be responsible for supplying miscellaneous materials (i.e., pens, paper,
notepads, etc.) incidental to service, including safety materials needed or required to
perform service, at no additional charge to the State.
D. The State will not pay for fees not listed on Exhibit B, Attachment 1, Cost Sheet (i.e.,
travel, freight, trip, tax, and/or gas surcharges, etc.).
E. The State does not guarantee the amount of work or services that may be requested
from the Contractor. The State reserves the right to use other venues of its
discretion. This is not an exclusive agreement.
F. The estimated number of hours provided in Exhibit B, Attachment 1 Cost Sheet is only
an estimate. The State reserves the right to increase or decrease the amount based on
actual need of services but not exceed the total amount of the contract.
G. An OAH Proceeding can include a determination of competence of a wide range of
professions (e.g., physicians and other medical professionals, certified public
accountants, engineers, contractors) and determination of eligibility for services or
appropriate services for children, adults, and students with disabilities. OAH may
provide Contractor with a list of common terms and acronyms for the purpose of
familiarizing ASL interpreters with OAH events. Contractor is expected to provide ASL
language services that include awareness of technical and disability terminology, in
addition to abiding by all requirements set forth in this Agreement, including all exhibits.
H. OAH presently uses Zoom for videoconference events, and secondarily Microsoft Teams
but may also utilize other communication methods, such as live-stream webinar, other
videoconferencing applications, chat, etc. Contractor shall ensure that assigned ASL
interpreters have the required videoconference software or applications.
I. Building Security:
1) The State shall have and exercise full and complete control over granting, denying,
withholding or terminating building clearances for Contractor’s personnel.
2) Depending on the location of the hearing, Contractor’s staff may be required to check
in with building security at the building’s main entrance or reception, where they may
be required to provide a valid State of California issued identification. In the event
the building security or reception issues Contractor’s personnel a temporary pass,
the temporary pass shall be worn while performing services in the building and on
building’s grounds and returned at the end of each day.

6. ORDERING INFORMATION
A. When work assignments are identified, OAH shall contact the contractors in the order
identified in Exhibit A, Attachment 2, Order of Contractors.
1) Primary Contractor – OAH shall request services from the Primary Contractor first. If
the Primary Contractor does not respond to the service request within twenty-four
(24)hours and/or cannot complete the work described in the service request, OAH
shall then send the service request to the Secondary Contractor.
2) Secondary Contractor – OAH shall request services from the Secondary Contractor
second. If the Secondary Contractor does not respond to the service request within
twenty-four (24) hours OAH may deem the Secondary Contractor unable to provide
services.
7. SERVICE CATEGORIES
A. In-Person ASL interpreting – the ASL interpreters will be in the same room as
individuals who are in need of ASL interpreting services.
B. VRI ASL interpreting - ASL interpreting will be done remotely in the method required
by OAH, such as live-stream webinar, videoconference, and/or chat. Contractor’s VRI
services include all labor, tools, materials, equipment, supervision and other
expenditures necessary to provide the services described herein.
8. SCHEDULING DETAILS
A. Whenever possible, OAH shall provide at least three (3) calendar days’ notice to
Contractor, by email request, for ASL interpreter services. The request shall include:
1) OAH requestor’s name, email address and phone number,
2) type of service requested (ASL interpreter)
3) nature of the proceeding (e.g. mediation, prehearing conference, hearing, etc.),
4) date(s), time, and, if in-person, the location of hearing,
5) access or security requirements,
6) name of assigned ALJ (if assigned), and
7) OAH case number
B. ASL Interpreter Services Requests
1) Within 24 hours of receipt of a request for services, Contractor shall reply by email to
the OAH Requestor confirming receipt of the request.
2) Contractor shall email the OAH Requestor when Contractor has assigned the ASL
interpreters for the requested service. The email shall include the name, email
address and telephone number of each of the assigned ASL interpreter Contractor
shall confirm assignment of the ASL interpreters no later than four (4) full business
days before the date of the event for which the assignment is needed, unless OAH
has requested the ASL interpreters less than four business days before the event.
3) Contractor shall try to assign the same ASL interpreters to multi-day events.
C. In the event of a rush, OAH may receive requests for ASL interpreting services the
evening before the hearing or the day of the hearing. The Contractor’s response time
frame will be identified in the service request (i.e. confirm or deny the request within a
couple hours).

D. Scheduled events are subject to change. The OAH Contract Administrator or OAH
Designated Representative and Contractor shall mutually agree in writing to modify
scheduled events, as needed, to reasonably accommodate the completion of the
proceeding.
9. PERFORMANCE DETAILS
A. Contractor shall provide ASL interpreters to interpret spoken English to ASL and/or ASL
to spoken English.
B. Contractor is responsible for ensuring the quality and accuracy of all ASL interpretering
services.
C. After five (5) hours of work, ASL interpreters are required to take an unpaid lunch break
of at least 30 minutes.
D. No assignment may be scheduled for less than two (2) hours. Assignments can be
scheduled and paid in one hour increments after the minimum two (2) hours.
E. Due to the length of appointments, two (2) ASL interpreters will be required for all
appointments.
F. ASL interpreters must not disclose privileged communications between counsel and
client to any person.
G. ASL interpreters must not give legal advice to parties and witnesses, nor recommend
specific attorneys or law firms.
H. ASL interpreters must maintain an impartial, professional relationship with all court
officers, attorneys, parties, and witnesses and accurately interpret the proceedings.
I. ASL interpreters will accurately interpret the participant’s statements and relay the
message in its entirety with the meaning preserved throughout the
conversation. Information will not be edited or deleted which may erroneously change
the meaning of the participant’s statements.
J. ASL interpreters will wear business attire to OAH proceedings. Will refrain from wearing
items such as jeans, and shorts, and for in person events, tennis shoes.
10. REPORTS
A. Contractor shall provide an annual usage report to the OAH Contract Administrator. The
annual usage report must be inclusive of all service requests made by OAH using this
Agreement that resulted in a charge for a service from Contractor, including, but not
limited to, VRI ASL services, In-person ASL services and cancellations. The report shall
be emailed to the OAH Contract Administrator by July 10 for the previous Fiscal.

SPECIAL TERMS AND CONDITIONS
1. STANDARD CONDITIONS OF SERVICE
A. Contractor will abide by all State and Federal laws in performance of this contract.
B. The Contractor shall maintain all license(s) required by law for accomplishing any work
required with this agreement. In the event any license(s) expire at any time during the
term of this agreement, Contractor agrees to provide to the State a copy of the renewed
license(s) within thirty (30) days following the expiration date. In the event the
Contractor fails to keep in effect at all times all required license(s), the State may, in
addition to any other remedies it may have, terminate this agreement upon occurrence
of such event.
C. The Contractor certifies that it has appropriate systems and controls in place to ensure
that State funds will not be used in the performance of this Contract for the acquisition,
operation or maintenance of computer software in violation of copyright laws.
D. If signing this contract as a sole proprietor, Contractor certifies that it is not an alien that
is ineligible for state and local benefits, as defined in Subtitle B of the Personal
Responsibility and Work Opportunity Act (8 U.S.C. § 1601 et seq.).
E. Pursuant to Public Contract Code section 10295.4, persons or companies identified as
the largest tax delinquents by the Franchise Tax Board (FTB) or the California
Department of Tax and Fee Administration (CDTFA) are ineligible to enter into any
contract with the state for non-IT goods or services. Any contract entered into in
violation of section 10295.4 is void and unenforceable.
F. If contract activities include collection of organic waste, the Contractor must be aware
and adhere to Public Resources Code § 42649.1 et. seq. concerning organic waste
recycling requirements. Organic waste includes: food waste, green waste, landscape
and pruning waste, nonhazardous wood waste, and food-soiled paper waste that is
mixed in with food waste.
G. The Contractor's, and any subcontractor's, own data center or cloud computing, where
data may be stored, must be physically located in the continental United States. Remote
access to data from outside the continental United States is prohibited.
2. EXCISE TAX: The State of California is exempt from Federal Excise Taxes, and no
payment will be made for any taxes levied on employees' wages.

subject to thirty (30) days written notice to the Contractor.

that the Contractor fails to meet the terms, conditions, and/or responsibilities of the
contract. In this instance, the contract termination shall be effective as of the date
indicated on the State’s notification to the Contractor.

5. SAFEGUARDS:
A. The Contractor shall develop and maintain an information privacy and security
program that includes the implementation of administrative, technical, and physical
safeguards appropriate to the size and complexity of the Contractor's operations
and the nature and scope of its activities. The information privacy and security
program shall reasonably and appropriately protect the confidentiality, integrity, and
availability of the PHI that it creates, receives, maintains, or transmits; and prevent
the use or disclosure of PHI other than as provided for by this Agreement. The
Contractor shall provide the DSH with information concerning such safeguards as
the DSH may reasonably request from time to time.
B. The Contractor shall implement administrative, technical, and physical safeguards
to ensure the security of the DSH information on portable electronic media (e.g.,
floppy disks and CD-ROM) and in paper files. Administrative safeguards to be
implemented shall include, but are not limited to training, instructions to employees,
and policies and procedures regarding the HIPAA Privacy Rule. Technical
safeguards to be implemented must comply with the HIPAA Security Rule and
Subpart C of part 164 of the HIPAA regulations with respect to electronic PHI, and
shall include, but are not limited to, role-based access, computer passwords, timing
out of screens, storing laptop computers in a secure location (never leaving the
equipment unattended at workplace, home or in a vehicle) and encryption.
Physical safeguards to be implemented shall include, but are not limited to, locks
on file cabinets, door locks, partitions, shredders, and confidential destruct.

However, if return or destruction is not feasible, Contractor shall continue to

that is in the possession of the Contractor, its subcontractor(s), or its agent(s).
Notwithstanding this section, OAH shall maintain records in accordance with its
approved record retention schedule.
